references.text: God reveals himself to Abram as El Shaddai and promises to make him very numerous. The same divine name and promise of fertility as in Gen 28:3.
God reveals himself as El Shaddai to Jacob and says, 'Be fruitful and become numerous; a congregation of peoples (kehal ammim) shall come from you' – a direct parallel to the blessing in 28:3.
Jacob reminds Joseph that El Shaddai appeared to him in Luz and blessed him with fertility and the promise to become a congregation of peoples – a direct reference back to the event in Gen 28:3.
The foundational promise of fertility: 'Be fruitful and multiply.' The words 'yafrekha veyarbekha' (make you fruitful and numerous) in 28:3 draw upon this original blessing motif.
Paul shows that all nations are blessed through Abraham's faith, which can be seen as a fulfillment of the promise that Jacob would become 'a congregation of peoples.'
Direct retelling and confirmation of the same covenant promise of nations and kings to Jacob.
The original covenant with Abraham (17:6) as the theological basis for Jacob's blessing in 28:3.
A contrast that clarifies that the promise of kings and many nations is unique to Jacob's line, unlike Ishmael's twelve princes.
Direct reference to and confirmation of the covenant promise in 28:3 at Jacob's deathbed.
